# Overview of this document {.unnumbered}

This document presents a reproducible computational workflow for the analysis and synthesis of cross-referencing information for Tasmanian terrestrial and transitional ecosystems. Cross-referencing aims to elucidate explicit, evidence-based relationships between units of ecosystem classifications that represent comparable entities [@IUCN_2025; see @sec-process].

The repository serves a **dual purpose**:

1. **Analytical workflow documentation** (this Quarto book, authored in `docs-src/`): documents every conceptual and computational step—from source alignment and lookup-table preparation through validation, multi-round expert-elicitation analysis, and synthesis—using the [`ecoSynthesis`](https://github.com/Ecosystem-Indicators-Workflows/ecoSynthesis) R package [@ecoSynthesis_pkg] alongside repository-specific helper scripts.
2. **Standalone spatial and tabular output generation** (kept separate in `scripts/` and summarised in @sec-outputs): executes computationally heavier vector unions, rasterisation, and Zenodo dataset packaging without slowing down or repeating calculations inside the documentation workflow.

In this workflow, the source classification is the TASVEG 5.0 dataset [@TASVEG_5; @KitchenerHarris_2013], whose technical manual and fire-attributes lookup table define 159 mapping units (156 mapped as polygons across mainland Tasmania and surrounding islands), most of which represent ecological vegetation communities (see @sec-source). These vegetation communities are aligned with the ecosystem concept of the target classification, the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology (IUCN GET; @Keith_2022; see @sec-alignment), specifically at Level 3 (Ecosystem Functional Groups, EFGs).

The main body of the document is organised into three parts:

- **Part I — Preparation**: Builds formal lookup tables for both classifications (@sec-lookup), ingests heterogeneous membership tables from five expert interpreters across two elicitation rounds (@sec-input-memb), validates and cleans membership records (@sec-valid), and explores completeness, duplicates, and group-level patterns (@sec-exploration).
- **Part II — Analysis**: Quantifies inter-interpreter agreement (pairwise similarity/dissimilarity), target usage, and within-interpreter uncertainty (normalised Shannon's entropy) in Round 1 (@sec-round-one) and Round 2 (@sec-round-two), and evaluates convergence and remaining conceptual disagreement between rounds (@sec-between-rounds).
- **Part III — Synthesis**: Consolidates Round 2 memberships under four synthesis strategies (@sec-synthesis), computes unweighted and membership-weighted area summaries (@sec-areas), and explains how tabular syntheses connect to spatial raster and vector outputs (@sec-maps).

Appendices provide a glossary of cross-referencing terminology, a reference on tabular membership formats (@sec-formats), R session and benchmarking notes (@sec-reproducibility), and an overview table summarising the status of all published, draft, and in-development workflow outputs (@sec-outputs).

This online document is a joint output of the ARDC "Ecosystem Indicators Workflows" (EIW) project and the ARC Industry Laureate Fellowship Project "Foundations for leading the nature positive ecosystem conservation agenda".

You can use the links on the left to navigate through the different sections of this resource.

::: {.callout-note}
## Target ecosystem types
- All terrestrial ecosystems of Tasmania.
- Selected palustrine wetland and other transitional ecosystems of Tasmania.
:::

## Contributions

MGT led the expert elicitation process. MGT, DAK, AL, AK, and JB contributed membership tables for cross-referencing. JRFP led the technical documentation of all sections of the online document. JRFP, EG, and ARS contributed scripts and `ecoSynthesis` package functions across all sections.

## Reproducibility statement

This resource uses Bash and R for data download, preparation, analysis, and synthesis, and is rendered as a Quarto book following FAIR data and research software principles [@Wilkinson_2016; @Barker_2022]. All analytical steps in the documentation are reproducible from the tracked expert elicitation tables (`xrefdata/`) and publicly available TASVEG 5.0 spatial data (`gisdata/`). Standalone spatial output scripts are separated in `scripts/` so computationally expensive rasterisation and vector-union steps are not repeated unnecessarily when updating the documentation. Instructions for environment setup, benchmarking logs, and FAIR assessment notes are provided in @sec-reproducibility and @sec-outputs.

## Statement on AI use {.unnumbered}

Generative AI assistance (Google Antigravity / Gemini) was used during version `0.0.6` to assist with refining narrative context, drafting code-block explanations, auditing overlaps between repository helper scripts and the `ecoSynthesis` package, adding exploratory analysis blocks (heatmaps and entropy metrics), formatting bibliographic entries, and compiling the outputs status table. All underlying expert elicitation data, ecological interpretations, workflow design decisions, code execution checks, and final editorial responsibility remain entirely with the human authors.
